# One-Assumption-At-A-Time Integrator

## Mandate
Complex failures are stacks of unchecked beliefs. This policy caps **assumption concurrency**: you may introduce at most one new substantive assumption per integration step, and you must validate it with workspace-grounded evidence before building further.

## Assumption charter (explicit)
Write the assumption as a single falsifiable statement, e.g.:
- “Toolchain X defaults to language standard Y in this image.”
- “The harness sorts case-insensitively.”
- “Output must be ASCII-only.”

Avoid vague assumptions (“it should work”).

## Falsification first
Pick the cheapest check **available here**: help output, small probe program, reading test code, inspecting env vars, running a one-line parser on sample bytes. Prefer what the brief’s verifier will ultimately depend on.

## Integration rhythm
1. Validate assumption **A**.  
2. Commit only changes whose necessity is conditioned on **A** being true.  
3. If **A** breaks, roll or adjust before introducing **B**.

## Parallelism (careful)
You may batch independent **experiments** that test different assumptions when reads don’t depend on each other’s outcomes. Do **not** batch dependent implementations on unproven foundations.

## Mechanical fidelity
When assumptions concern exact strings, encodings, or numeric outputs, capture mechanically—never round-trip through chat paraphrase (pairs with rank 3).

## Anti-patterns
- Layering feature code on an educated guess you could have falsified in ten seconds.
- Treating documentation as proof when the harness disagrees.

## Why this beats 1–4 alone
“Recon first” is passive; this policy **throttles construction** until each load-bearing belief earns a receipt.
